newsitem.title: ITALY: Treasury says ratings agencies deny Italy plans.
newsitem.headline: Treasury says ratings agencies deny Italy plans.

text.p: A senior Italian Treasury official said on Friday that Moody's Investors Service, IBCA and Standard & Poor's had all denied any plans to downgrade Italy's ratings.
There were rumours in Italian financial markets that one rating agency was planning a downgrade.
"According to our information at the Treasury, the three rating agencies have denied that there will be a revision of current ratings," the official said.
Moody's and IBCA earlier declined to comment on the rumours.
Standard & Poor's said Italy was not on CreditWatch and therefore a rating change was unlikely.
A spokesman for Moody's said Italy has a Aa3 sovereign ceiling rating for foreign currency bonds, notes and bank deposits.
